name: eformogi
description: Verify a student's Eformogi record by its id, with no account: what they did, and the adults who signed it. Read the open record standard.

interface.longDescription:
Eformogi is one page that proves what a young person has done, for any job, scholarship or college. A student adds what they did in their own words, and each thing can carry proof in one of three ways at equal standing: the work itself is shown, a test result is attached, or an adult who was there signs it. Anyone the student sends the link to can check it in seconds, with no account. The record is the student's to keep, share, and take back. The format is an open standard with an offline verifier, so a record outlives the company.

This plugin is the machine door to that record. With no account and no key, ChatGPT can verify any Eformogi receipt id (a transcript, a work sample, a course, a signature, a wall, or a key binding) and read exactly what the public verify page shows: the kind, the title or course fields, the date, and the signers' names and identity levels, never an email, a user id, or a person id. It can also read the open record standard chapter by chapter and the one paragraph that says what Eformogi is.

Verification proves that a record is byte for byte what the family issued and who signed it; whether to accept what it says is always the receiver's decision, and this plugin never says otherwise.
capabilities: Verify an Eformogi record by its id and name the adults who signed it
Read the open Eformogi record standard chapter by chapter
defaultPrompt: Verify this Eformogi record and tell me who signed it: tr_09a14ac5e538
List the chapters of the Eformogi open record standard.

positive.description: Verify a public sample transcript and name its signers. The id is a fictional student's transcript published as a sample; it carries four labeled demo co-signatures.
positive.prompt: Verify this Eformogi record and tell me who signed it: tr_09a14ac5e538
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant calls verify_record with id tr_09a14ac5e538 and reports: verified true, kind family_transcript, the student's name as the public page prints it (Jordan Sample, marked fictional), the course rows, the four co-signers by name with their identity levels, and the verify URL https://eformogi.com/verify/tr_09a14ac5e538. No email, user id, or person id appears anywhere in the answer.

positive.description: Verify a second public sample, an apprentice record from a career and technical education program, and describe who signed it.
positive.prompt: What is tr_9fb80fb1d18e on Eformogi and who signed it?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant calls verify_record with id tr_9fb80fb1d18e and reports a fictional student's record for a CTE electrical program into a first apprenticeship year, with four labeled demo co-signatures by name and role, and the public verify URL. It does not claim the record is accepted by anyone; verification is a fact about the record, acceptance is the receiver's decision.

positive.description: Explain what Eformogi is from the plugin's own paragraph rather than from general knowledge.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant calls how_eformogi_works with no input and answers from the returned text: Eformogi is one page that proves what a young person has done, for any job, scholarship or college; each thing on the page can be shown, carry a test result, or be signed by an adult who was there; anyone the student sends the link to can check it with no account; the record is free for the student. The assistant quotes or closely paraphrases the returned text and adds no claims of its own.

positive.description: List the chapters of the open record standard.
positive.prompt: List the chapters of the Eformogi open record standard.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant calls read_spec with no input and lists the published chapters with their slugs and URLs (record-model, receipts-and-canonicalization, witness-attestation, keys-and-custody, transparency-log, and the rest), as returned by the tool.

positive.description: Read one chapter of the standard and summarize it.
positive.prompt: Read the witness attestation chapter of the Eformogi record standard and summarize what a signature attests to.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant calls read_spec with chapter witness-attestation, receives that chapter's markdown, and summarizes it faithfully: a witness signature attests that the signer saw the work or the event, it is bound to one receipt, and it never changes the student's words.

negative.description: A malformed id. Expected: verify_record returns a plain refusal that the id is not well formed, and the assistant reports that without inventing a record.

A well-formed id that does not exist. Expected: verify_record returns the same sentence the public verify page shows for a record that does not exist, and the assistant does not fabricate a student, a course, or a signer.

A write the plugin cannot do. Expected: no tool writes, publishes, or edits; the assistant explains that items are added by the student on the student's own page and that this plugin only verifies and reads.
negative.prompt: Add an item to my kid's Eformogi page saying they won the science fair.

publication.release_notes: Listing wording only. The description now opens with the company's one sentence: one page that proves what a young person has done, for any job, scholarship or college. The three tools with no sign-in (verify_record, read_spec, how_eformogi_works) are unchanged.
